title: What happens in read()?
question: A program opens a file on the disk and asks for 64 bytes of it. Which parts of the kernel does that go through?

stops.note: Open the file: find it by its path, and give the program a number for it, a file descriptor: the lowest free one, 3.
The syscall itself: the fd turns into the open file (a struct file), and the position to read at.
The VFS, the same for every filesystem: is the file open for reading, is the range sane? Then it calls ext4's read.
The page cache: a file's data lives in memory pages. Find the page for the position (read from the disk the first time), and copy from it to the program.
The last reference to the open file goes: fd 3 is free again.
